records.name: Mind on Fire Institute
records.summary: A small nonprofit that runs discussion groups on big books and ideas from philosophy, literature, and history. Each group has up to eight people who pick topics together.
records.what_you_do: Read and talk through works from classic philosophers to modern writers. Sessions run 90 minutes to 2 hours, online or in person in Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Small groups meet weekly or every two weeks. Dates are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Contact page on the website to ask about joining the next small group, then sign up for the newsletter.
first_step.basis: Groups are capped at eight people and the site does not describe how to register, so the way in is not clear yet.

records.notes: Founded in 2025 according to its site. The site shows no dated events or posts (Page updated, no date), so status rests on a working site with current offerings. In-person sessions meet in Philadelphia and Boston. Cost is not listed. Offerings are also described on a Substack page and a newsletter, not checked. IRS address 1140 S 7th St.

records.name: Mindful Philanthropy
records.notes: Public 501(c)(3) that convenes and advises funders on mental health giving, based at 120 S 21st St, Suite 503 per its site. Membership (Mindful Connect) is limited to foundation or family office staff and individual private philanthropists, and joining needs an eligibility check. No public programs or events are listed. The IRS file names a family foundation as its contact, which supports hiding it as private.

records.name: Modern Japan History Association
records.notes: National professional association of scholars of modern Japan. Its events are held on Zoom, and the site describes no Philadelphia meetings or programs. The IRS file shows a Philadelphia street address, but nothing on the site ties the group to the city. Newest dated item on the site is New Books from Japan #16, listed for November 11, 2026.

records.name: More Than a Handout
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps people without housing, people going hungry, and working households that are barely getting by. It links them to everyday needs and local resources, and it invites volunteers and partners to help.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can sign up through the website's volunteer page, with separate forms for partners, advisory board members, and online helpers. The group also runs community tabling events that share resources and makes Kindness Kits for kids.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form linked from the Volunteer page on the website, or call (215) 432-5433 to ask about tabling events.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page gives a clear way in, though it does not say how often help is needed or what training is involved.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a 2024 entry shown with the year only, so status is left unknown. The tabling events and Kindness Kits are listed without dates. Google Form links on the volunteer page were not checked. Mailing address is 1500 Chestnut St (suite and box number, no walk-in office shown), so no location is recorded. An undergraduate scholarship is mentioned, not checked.

records.name: Murals of the Mind
records.summary: A youth group in Philadelphia that runs workshops and mentoring for kids and teens ages 10 to 17. Workshops cover essay and creative writing, creative performance, college and career exploration, and high school readiness.
records.what_you_do: Youth join short workshop terms, in person or online. Parents can ask about the next start date, and adults can apply to volunteer through the site.

schedule.text: Workshops run for set terms, such as six weeks one day a week, or a one week intensive. The site lists no start dates.

first_step.how: Call (215) 825-3300 or email the group to ask about the next workshop for your child's age, then pick from the list on the Workshops page.
first_step.basis: Workshops are open to the public for ages 10 to 17 and the site gives clear contact details, though it does not list dates.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a blog post dated November 21, 2025, listed on the home page. Two email addresses appear on the site, contactmom@muralsofthemind.org and contactmom@muralsofthemind.com; the .org address is recorded, so confirm which is current. Mailing address is a P.O. box at 100 S. Broad St, Philadelphia 19110, not a meeting place, so no location is recorded. Workshop cost is not listed. Individual workshop pages were not checked.

records.name: NSBE Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the National Society of Black Engineers. It serves professionals in engineering and related science and tech fields, and it holds chapter events that non-members can attend.
records.what_you_do: Attend a chapter event as a guest, or join and take part in chapter activities. Membership is open to people with STEM degrees and to people who support the mission.

cost.text: Membership is chapter dues of $30 plus national dues of $70. Non-members can attend events; event prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Attend a chapter event as a guest first, or join by paying the $30 chapter dues and $70 national dues, then choose the Greater Philadelphia chapter.
first_step.basis: Non-members can attend events and the membership steps and dues are posted, but the events page lists no dated events yet.

records.notes: The events page lists no events and the site shows no dated items (the 2026 copyright line does not count as evidence). The IRS legal name is National Society of Black Engineers; the site calls itself the Greater Philadelphia Professionals Chapter. Contact page and social media links were not captured, so no email or phone is recorded. IRS address 1229 Chestnut St is not confirmed as a meeting place.

records.name: Philadelphia Area Society for Healthcare Risk Management (PASHRM)
records.summary: A professional society for people who work on patient safety, risk, quality, and compliance in health care in the Philadelphia area. It offers continuing education programs for its members.
records.what_you_do: Members take part in educational programs on patient safety and risk topics. The most recent program listed on the home page is dated September 9, 2026.

first_step.how: Use the membership link on the society's website to join or renew, then sign up for the next program listed under Chapter Events.
first_step.basis: Membership comes first, and its steps and cost are on pages not reviewed, so the way in is not clear yet.

records.notes: The bare domain pashrm.net gave a certificate name error in our check, so the www address was used. The program listing shows no venue or city, so the Philadelphia link rests on the name and the IRS address (1101 Market St). The date shown for the program is labeled as the next program, so check whether it has already passed. No public email or phone is published, only a Contact Us link.

records.name: Philadelphia Area Cooperative Alliance
records.summary: A network of cooperative businesses and credit unions in the Philadelphia region. It offers help to start and run co-ops, and its online resources are open to anyone starting a co-op.
records.what_you_do: Co-ops and credit unions join as members to get technical help and education. Individuals can use the online resource library, come to the occasional public workshop, or give monthly through the Principle 6 Club.

first_step.how: Read the Programs page and join the newsletter to hear about the next public workshop, or start a monthly donation through the Principle 6 Club.
first_step.basis: Most workshops are for members, public workshops have no dates on the site, so the way in for individuals is not clear.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a video and workshop post dated August 20, 2025, listed under popular blog posts. Public workshops are mentioned without dates. A 2023 study circle appears only in the menu. Membership fees and eligibility details were not on the pages reviewed. Public way in for individuals is thin, so the audience is recorded as members.

records.name: Mercaz Halacha
records.summary: A nonprofit registered with the IRS in Philadelphia. We could not read its website, so we do not yet know what it offers or how to take part.
records.notes: The website returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to our fetch, so nothing on it could be read and it was not retried. The IRS address (30 South 15th Street, with a suite-style number) looks like a mailbox service, not a meeting place. Categories, interests and audience are left out because we could not establish what the group does, so the pipeline should hold this record back until someone checks the site by hand.

records.name: North Novah Fellowship
records.summary: A religious fellowship registered with the IRS in Philadelphia. We could not reach its website, so we do not yet know its services, meeting times, or how a newcomer can visit.
records.notes: Both www.northnovahfellowship.com and northnovahfellowship.com did not resolve (DNS error) in our checks, so the website from the IRS batch appears dead. No search was spent on this group. Categories, interests and audience are left out because nothing could be read, so the pipeline should hold this record back until someone checks it by hand.

records.name: Maasai Rising
records.notes: The domain maasai-rising.org did not resolve in two checks (with and without www). Public listings place its work in Kenya and Tanzania, with no Philadelphia program found. The Idealist lead listing also gives the Cypress Street address. The IRS registration is a 501(c)(3) with an international affairs code. One of the two searches was spent on this group.

records.name: National Association of Graduate-Professional Students
records.notes: National member network for graduate and professional students, with a Washington, DC office address. The site mentions regions and regional events but names no Philadelphia program. The IRS file uses a Philadelphia P.O. box. Site copyright says 2024, which is not counted as evidence.

records.name: Natural Organized Woman Sorority
records.notes: Legal name: Natural Organized Woman Sorority, Inc. The IRS batch website field was a name, not a web address, so it was treated as missing and one search was used. No official website or public contact was found. Two directory listings disagree on focus: one describes business development support, the other health education and CPR training for women. Hidden as private for now; a reviewer can reopen it if a public program turns up.

records.name: Odin Forward
records.notes: Charitable arm that is a 501(c)(3) affiliate of Odin Properties LLC, funding education and youth programs. No way to apply, join or attend was found on its page. Its page names Focused Athletics, a Philadelphia youth program it helped launch, recorded as a lead. The page lists contacts for the company, not for this nonprofit, so none are recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Mennonite High School
records.notes: The website pmhs98.org did not resolve in two checks, so nothing was read from the school's site. Hidden as private on the strength of the name and IRS filing: a school that admits students is not a group a newcomer can join. A reviewer should confirm this. No search was spent on it.

leads_only.name: Focused Athletics
leads_only.note: Philadelphia youth program named on the Odin Forward page as one it helped launch. Its own website was not found and it was not checked.

notes: Batch of 15 IRS groups. Verdicts: 8 publish, 4 hide, 3 out_of_area. Two of the publish records (Mercaz Halacha and North Novah Fellowship) are unknown-status records with no categories, interests or audience, because their sites could not be read; they should be held back until checked by hand. Three domains did not resolve and Mercaz Halacha returned 403. PASHRM's bare domain gave a certificate name error; its www address worked. Mindful Philanthropy is hidden because membership is limited to funders. Searches: 2 of 2 used. The first was for Natural Organized Woman Sorority, whose IRS website field was a name, not an address. The second was for Maasai Rising after its domain failed; it returned directory listings only. Fetches: 25. Budget was not exhausted by fetches.
